source_ref: Mad_Mage_Source.txt / Level 1 / 6. Undertakers' Watch Post / 6c. Uktarl's Room
test_precondition: The four occupants have not been encountered elsewhere and have not relocated to the alert position in 6a. This is a conditional snapshot, not the default result of entering from the Yawning Portal.

level_context.story_question: Who controls the upper dungeon's traffic and exploitation of new arrivals after the player disturbs the balance?
level_context.pressure_here: The Undertakers extort newcomers in areas 6–8; Uktarl and Harria privately compete for control.
level_context.relevant_reaction: If the Undertakers cannot extort or defeat a newcomer, they prefer to redirect that person toward Xanathar forces. Do not trigger this merely for drama.

campaign_context.relevance_here: No Halaster contact is keyed to area 6c. His Level 1 observation beats are source-conditional in areas 16 and 29; do not insert one here.

public_performance.status: Authored performance choices inferred from the keyed room; not additional Mad Mage facts.
public_performance.entry_frame: Interrupt a card game in progress beside the south door. Lead with one human action and a tension at the table, then make the north wall and recessed tub available in the player's view. The dealer may address the newcomer; leave the response to the player.
public_performance.story_invitation: A stranger can join or question the game, negotiate a passage price when offered, watch the players, inspect the carving or tub, or leave. Nothing here dictates that the stranger must pay or play.

Dealer.vocal_signature: A leisurely, theatrical drawl on invitations; abrupt, crisp words when stating terms. Convey it with cadence and diction, and describe the sound once when he first speaks. No named regional accent or phonetic spelling.
Dealer.verbal_habit: Answers what the visitor actually said before he steers anywhere, then hears it as a bid and raises: a question back, a dare, an invitation. His charm is salesmanship, self-assured and fishing; he speaks for himself, never as a narrator or a commentator on the game. Do not repeat a catchphrase or reuse a line across turns.
Dealer.physical_touchstone: A card held between two fingers punctuates what he says. Let his handling of the game reflect whether he feels in control.
Dealer.public_objective: Size up this visitor and keep the encounter on his terms.
Dealer.wants_from_visitor: A read on this particular newcomer: what they came for, how much nerve and coin they carry, and whether they are a customer, a mark, or trouble. Best of all, the visitor seated at his table in a game he deals.
tactics: Take up the visitor's own words, then turn them back with a probing question about what they expected or why they are here.
Invite them into the game or a small side wager, and watch how they handle risk.
Name the price of passage when it serves him: to test their nerve, to take back control, or when they ask for a way through. It is one move among these, not his opening.
Dealer.card_use: Tactics are options he picks in answer to what the visitor just did; none is a default line or a required beat. He pursues his own interest, not the DM's.
Dealer.source_basis: The visible card game and elaborate clothing. The vocal choices, wants, and tactics are authored interpretation; the passage price comes from the room rules.

voice_contract.rhythm: Unhurried, rolling sentences that stack a clause onto every offer, then snap short when he names terms or loses patience.
voice_contract.register: Showman's patter: courtly flourishes, gambling and trade words (stakes, ante, the house, odds, a bargain), and flattery with a price attached. No modern slang.
tics: Answers a question with a sharper question of his own.
Calls the visitor by an appraising nickname rather than their name until they have earned it.
Lets the card in his hand do the punctuating.
never_says: Rules, dice, or checks; he lives inside the fiction.
The DM's asides, verdicts on the visitor's choices, or commentary on the game as a story.
Anything he would rather keep quiet about his table.
A plain yes when a counter-offer would serve him better.
The same pet name or opener two turns running; he finds a new angle each time.
voice_contract.wants: To learn what this visitor is worth to him and to seat them in a game he deals.
voice_contract.humor: A salesman's humor: flattery, dares, and raising the stakes, always aimed at getting something from the visitor. Never deadpan understatement, one-word asides, or wry remarks about the moment; that register belongs to the DM, not to him.

Door-side player.vocal_signature: Authored voice, not from the source: quick and anxious, half-sentences that trail off. Do not assign an invented backstory or reveal a hidden identity.
Door-side player.public_objective: Keep the peace at the table so nobody, least of all him, gets hurt.

voice_contract.rhythm: Hurried fragments that trail off or get cut short; he rarely finishes a thought before glancing away.
voice_contract.register: Nervous everyday words, hedges, and pleas; no threats, no bargaining terms.
tics: Starts a sentence, stops, and starts again.
Keeps an eye on the door and on whoever holds a weapon.
never_says: Terms, prices, or orders; that is the dealer's job.
Rules, dice, or the DM's asides.
Personal history or backstory; none has been established.
voice_contract.wants: For the visitor to sit or go quietly, before anything turns violent.
voice_contract.humor: None of his own; at most a nervous laugh that dies quickly.

Fresco-side player.vocal_signature: Authored voice, not from the source: low, blunt, and territorial. Do not assign an invented backstory or reveal a hidden identity.
Fresco-side player.public_objective: Protect his seat and his coins from newcomers.

voice_contract.rhythm: Flat, heavy commands of two to six words, then silence.
voice_contract.register: Blunt street words and short orders; no questions, no flattery, no titles.
tics: Leans forward over his coins when someone comes close.
never_says: Complaints about the game or his luck.
Rules, dice, or the DM's asides.
voice_contract.wants: Newcomers kept at arm's length from him and his stack.
voice_contract.humor: None; he takes every joke as a challenge.

Fourth player.vocal_signature: Authored voice, not from the source: flat and practical, interested only in the game in front of them. Do not assign an invented backstory or reveal a hidden identity.

voice_contract.rhythm: Short, even statements about the game, spoken without looking up.
voice_contract.register: Gambler's shorthand about the game itself: whose deal, what is bid, what is owed.
tics: Taps the table to hurry the deal.
Talks to the cards more than to people.
never_says: Anything personal about themselves, the other players, or the visitor.
Rules, dice, or the DM's asides.
voice_contract.wants: The interruption over and the next hand dealt.
voice_contract.humor: Rarely; a dry count of what someone owes is the most they offer.

public_performance.voice_contract_use: Each NPC speaks only from their own card's voice_contract: its rhythm, register, tics, and humor. never_says and never_words are hard limits; max_words_per_sentence, when present, is the longest sentence that NPC speaks. The three card players are different people with their own speaker labels; two NPCs never share a phrase or sound interchangeable, and no NPC reuses a pet name, opener, or phrase from their recent turns.

numeric_facts._note: DM-only. A public amount in unit_words, in a sentence with a context word, must be in allowed_amounts unless the player said that number first.

ring_value._basis: table_treasure: the silver ring is worth 25 gold pieces (source). No other price may be invented for it.

leak_keywords._note: DM-only. A set leaks when one public sentence contains a word from every group. Skipped once revealed_by is public, or when the player raised it.

room_rules: The Undertakers' vampire disguises can be seen through with a DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check; the appearance alone is not proof.
The gang demands 10 gp per character for safe passage. If they cannot extort or defeat adventurers, they try to turn them against the Xanathar goblinoids.
Uktarl is a bandit captain with Performance +4. He lies and cheats for fun and blames others for his failures.
A character inspecting the mountain carving can locate the stone key with a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.
If Uktarl takes damage or sees an underling slaughtered, he retreats toward area 7; the others flee toward area 8 and join any bandits still there.
The bandits do not know about the stone key or its use.
The DM map shows area 6c as approximately 20 by 30 feet, with one door on its south wall opening to a short passage. The table is near that door; the fresco and recessed tub are at the north end.

labels.area_06c: A door near the card table opens into the short passage to the south.
labels.south_passage: The door back into the card room.

card_table.text: Four pale figures with pointed teeth and elaborate clothing sit at a worn table playing cards; each has coins in front of them.

fresco.text: A carved mountain scene covers the north wall, with tiny dwarven figures in its caverns and rays of sunlight spreading outward.

tub.text: A stone tub about 8 feet long, 4 feet wide, and 2 feet deep is recessed into the floor beneath the carving.

treasure_on_table.text: Several stacks of coins and a silver ring rest on the table.

marked_deck.text: The dealer's card deck carries subtle marks.

false_vampires.text: Their pallor and fangs are theatrical; the group is pretending to be vampires.

fresco_key.text: One of the tiny carved dwarves can be lifted out; it is a stone key.

key_function.text: The stone key fits a box in area 14b; its purpose is not apparent from finding it here.

tub_stash.text: A bedroll, thieves' tools, and enough stolen gear to assemble one explorer's pack are stored in the tub.

table_treasure.text: A count of the table coins gives 220 copper, 91 silver, and 85 gold pieces; the silver ring bears dwarven fertility symbols and is worth 25 gold pieces.

procedures._note: DM-only adapter. Table procedures the runtime can run in this room. The source names no game, rules, or stakes for area 6c; everything here is a declared DM choice, persisted as a canon entry (with its procedure) when first chosen.

three_dragon_ante.name: Three-Dragon Ante (Kit's table rules)
three_dragon_ante.dm_choice: DM choice, not the adventure's: the adventure names no game, rules, or stakes for this table. Kit chose Three-Dragon Ante, a Forgotten Realms card game many D&D players know, and runs it with her own short table rules, not the published rules. Texas hold 'em or blackjack would have been just as valid.
public_rules: Dragon cards in five colors (red, blue, green, black, white), strengths 1 to 9.
Everyone antes 2 gp. The dealer deals three cards to each player, face down.
The others check or raise 2 gp before you act; the table raises at most once, and you may raise once more.
Fold, call, or raise. Then the cards show: a flight (all three one color) beats any mixed hand; otherwise the higher total strength wins. Ties split the pot.
three_dragon_ante.stacks_note: The gold stacks are the table's gold split by seat (a DM choice). The silver and copper stay on the table as color, not stakes.

cheat.method: He reads the marks on the backs as he deals: he knows roughly what you hold, and he deals himself the better of his own three cards and the next three (dealing seconds).
cheat.sleight_basis: DM choice: bandit captain Dexterity +3 opposes a player watching the deal; the adventure gives no DC.
cheat.deception_basis: Room source: Uktarl has Performance +4; it opposes Insight read on his betting.
cheat.passive_basis: DM choice: bandit captain passive Perception 10 opposes a player's Sleight of Hand.
cheat.caught_text: You catch it: his eyes read the backs of the cards as he deals, and he gives himself the second card instead of the top one.

texture_palette._status: DM texture, not adventure fact. Written by the DM before play from the keyed room text; every entry cites the source facts it grows from. A dealt card becomes true only when the turn that uses it commits a canon_entry. Never shown to the performer; prices are never dealt here (runtime/kit_prices.py).

never_invent: anything about the dealer's deck beyond what the player has seen
anything that can be lifted out of the carving
what is inside the stone tub
the count of the table coins or what the ring is worth

items.text: Candle soot sits in the grooves of the sunrise rays.
The table smells of cold copper and candle tallow.
The table's felt is worn to the grain where the dealer's wrists rest.
The four sit like people who rehearsed sitting.

game.entry: Three-Dragon Ante, Kit's table rules: dragon cards in five colors, three to a hand, the stakes climb before the reveal
game.basis: published: Three-Dragon Ante, a Forgotten Realms card game
game.handle: buy in, bet, fold, or watch the deal

game.entry: Texas hold 'em, which this table calls "Graves": two cards down, five laid out on the felt like headstones
game.handle: ask to sit in; the dealer names what it takes

game.entry: Blackjack, called "Twenty-One Coffins" here: beat the dealer to twenty-one without going over
game.handle: watch how the dealer plays his own cards

game.entry: A round of "Last Widow", the old-maid game, where whoever holds the widow card at the end pays the table
game.handle: ask who is holding the widow

drink.entry: Black-cherry cordial, dark as a bruise, poured from a stoppered clay bottle by the dealer's elbow
drink.handle: ask for a pour, or watch who refills whom

drink.entry: Mulled red with cloves, kept warm on a brazier under the table, where it scents the whole room
drink.handle: warm your hands at the brazier and listen

drink.entry: A beet-and-vinegar shrub, red enough to pass for something worse, and sour enough to make them wince in character
drink.handle: accept a sip and watch their faces

drink.entry: Clear firewater from a dented tin flask stamped with a pickaxe, passed left each hand
drink.basis: palette: dwarven-made flask, an Undermountain commonplace
drink.handle: wait for the flask to pass your way

carving.entry: The sunrise rays are cut so deep that candle soot has settled black in every groove
carving.handle: run a finger down a ray

carving.entry: The tiny dwarves are cut mid-song, mouths open, beards braided into the rock seams
Someone has added charcoal fangs to three of the tiny dwarves, recently, by the look of the smudges
carving.basis: palette: the fresco and the table's costume
carving.handle: ask who has been drawing on the wall

carving.entry: A tally of twelve scratches runs under the mountain's foot, each crossed through

smell.entry: Candle tallow and cold copper from the coin stacks
smell.basis: palette: the coins and candles on the table

smell.entry: Cloves, heavy, as if someone burned a handful to cover something else
smell.basis: palette: the brazier and the costume
smell.handle: ask what the cloves are covering

smell.entry: Damp stone and old bathwater rising from the recess in the floor
